## 01 · First Passage — PhD research: when a random walker first arrives (首达——博士研究：随机游走何时第一次到达)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/research/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/research/

Why one target can have two arrival peaks, and exactly when the second dies: a single-author paper submitted to Physical Review E (a physics journal).

Why it matters: First-passage times are everywhere a search has to succeed: a molecule finding a receptor, a signal crossing a network, a pest finding a trap (Chapter 07).

_Fig. 1 — A ring, one shortcut, and an arrival time that splits in two._

- 12 Jun 2026 – 2 Jul 2026 · **Why a second peak is born — and dies** (第二个峰为何出生，又为何消失) — Completed. The ring’s double peak became a threshold theory. In the diffusive limit the problem is Brownian motion on an interval with an interior sink that stands for the shortcut; the first-passage density is a signed mixture of spectral modes, and a second peak needs at least three of them. In the symmetric case, with the sink at the midpoint, the fold comes at a sink strength of about 3.0764, with exponents ½ and ³⁄₂. Five independent checks agree: exact lattice residues, Monte Carlo with 400,000 walkers, an exact channel decomposition, Brownian dynamics and finite two-dimensional lattices. Metrics: Critical strength, symmetric case ≈ 3.0764; Fold exponents 1/2 · 3/2.
- Sep 2024 – Sep 2025 · **MSc dissertation: first passage in confined random walks** (硕士论文：受限随机游走中的首达现象) — Completed. The MSc in Engineering Mathematics at Bristol (2024–25) finished with a Distinction (the top UK grade) and a dissertation titled ‘First-Passage Phenomena in Confined Random Walks: Finite-Size Effects, Exact Solutions, and Spatial Heterogeneity’. It asked how long a random walker takes to first reach a target on one-, two- and three-dimensional lattices, with and without defects, and set exact solutions against simulation. The code is public. It is the first place the walker got trapped in a box — and the question has not let go since. Metrics: Classification Distinction. Links: [Article (2026): paper, proofs, code](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/master-dissertation)
- 3 Nov 2025 · **PhD in Engineering Mathematics, University of Bristol** (布里斯托大学工程数学博士) — Ongoing. Role: PhD researcher, University of Bristol, School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology (SEMT). The PhD began on 3 November 2025 in the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology (SEMT) at the University of Bristol. The subject is first-passage time: how long a random walker takes to reach a target for the first time, and why the distribution of that time can split into two peaks. Over the first year the work has broadened to span stochastic processes and the evaluation of AI agents. The random walks moving across this page are the same kind of object the thesis studies.
- 28 Nov 2025 · **First PhD code: a ring with defects** (博士第一份代码：带缺陷的环) — Completed. Within four weeks of starting, a first prototype was specified and built: a Python simulation of a random walk on a one-dimensional ring with defects, with analysis scripts, parameter scans and a small web visualiser. One configuration already hinted at a two-humped first-passage histogram. It was a sketch rather than a result, and it was archived once the exact methods arrived — but it is the baby picture of the whole research line.
- 10 Dec 2025 · **Computing on the Isambard supercomputers** (在 Isambard 超算上计算) — Ongoing. From December 2025 the heavy computation ran on Isambard, the UK national AI supercomputers hosted in Bristol, as part of a university project on random walkers in disordered environments. Command-line automation syncs the code, submits jobs to the scheduler and fetches the results. Isambard-AI carried the encounter paper’s heavy runs from the lattice to the continuum limit — lattice ladders refined up to n = 33 and Brownian dynamics with 20 million walkers per release position — and Isambard 3 ran the large-scale checks for the fixed-budget paper in September 2026, including a census of 2 billion walkers. Metrics: Walkers in one census 2 billion.
- 21 Dec 2025 – 30 Dec 2025 · **Lazy rings with a shortcut: the bilingual reports** (带捷径的懒惰环：中英双语报告) — Completed. The ring studies were consolidated into bilingual reports: a lazy ring with a one-way shortcut, two neighbour kernels, scans over shortcut strength β and ring size N, Monte Carlo trajectory classes and tail diagnostics. The long-time tail turned out to be set by the spectral radius of the transient chain, and β* = 0.01 was the smallest shortcut strength at which both kernels meet the double-peak criterion. A suspicious plateau in one figure was traced to a truncation in the numerical inversion and fixed — the first of many bugs caught by refusing to trust a pretty curve. Links: [Report in the atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/en/reports/ring_lazy_jump_ext/)
- Jan 2026 – Jun 2026 · **From rings to two-dimensional lattices** (从环到二维格点) — Completed. In 2026 the question moved from rings to two-dimensional lattices — periodic, rectangular and reflecting domains, a membrane near the target, two competing targets, local bias fields and two-walker encounters. Of the 27 reports in the public research atlas, 13 belong to this lattice family. One finding: a membrane’s permeability mainly adds to the time spent after the crossing, which is why some geometries keep a clear double peak even with minimal bias. Metrics: Lattice reports 13. Links: [All reports](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/en/reports/)
- 25 Feb 2026 · **A public, bilingual research atlas** (公开的中英双语研究图谱) — Live. On 25–26 February 2026 the first-passage line got its own public website: a static research atlas in English and Chinese, with a continuous ‘book’ of eight chapters, a page for every report, a theory section, interactive figures and typeset mathematics. It maps 27 reports and tracks 130 claims back to their evidence. The repository behind it is organised ‘agent-first’ — one command-line tool, guardrail tests and a machine-readable report registry — so that people and AI agents can work on it in the same way. Metrics: Book chapters 8; Mapped reports 27; Tracked claims 130. Links: [Research atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/)
- 30 Mar 2026 · **BAMC 2026, Norwich** (BAMC 2026，诺里奇) — Attended. Attended the British Applied Mathematics Colloquium 2026 at the University of East Anglia in Norwich, which opened on 30 March 2026 — the first national applied-mathematics meeting of the PhD, and a first look at where first-passage questions sit within the wider field.
- 14 Apr 2026 – 15 Apr 2026 · **‘Hidden Routes in First-Passage Time’** (《首达时间中的隐藏路径》) — Deck published. A ten-minute talk for PhD students across SEMT, the School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology, given at its Ideas Exchange Day and built as a web slide deck inside the research atlas, with a live random-walk animation and figures regenerated from the research code. Its one-line thesis: a single target on a ring still produces a fast branch, a valley and a delayed branch once one directed shortcut is present. Deck and script are public in both languages. Metrics: Length 10 min · 9 slides. Links: [Talk (English)](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/en/talk/smet-phd/) · [Talk (Chinese)](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/cn/talk/smet-phd/)
- 28 May 2026 – 31 May 2026 · **Three ingredients of a double peak** (双峰的三个条件) — Completed. A 12-page brief pulled the year’s cases together — ring shortcuts, two-target lattices and exact two-walker encounter searches — and argued that a visible double peak needs three things at once: a balance between the masses of the fast and slow channels, well-separated timescales, and a valley deep enough to resolve. A second talk page on multi-timescale encounters, with a live two-dimensional hopping demo, joined the atlas on 31 May 2026. Links: [Encounter talk page](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/en/talk/multitimescale-encounter/)
- 9 Jun 2026 – 11 Jun 2026 · **The term that cancels** (那个会自己消失的项) — Completed. For a lazy ring with an antipodal shortcut, a ‘t·αᵗ’ term was suspected in the long-time tail of the first-passage distribution. It is not there. Three independent arguments show that its coefficient is identically zero: a partial-fraction sum rule; a trace of the term to an artefact of the generating-function inversion; and symmetry — the transient matrix is diagonalisable, so terms like t·λᵗ cannot occur for any parameters. Every identity was checked in 50-digit arithmetic and with exact rational kernels. Metrics: Independent proofs 3.
- Jul 2026 · **Working paper: spectral diagnostics for encounter–reaction models** (工作论文：相遇—反应模型的谱诊断) — Working paper. A single-author working paper on when two diffusing particles that react on contact produce more than one reaction-time peak in finite models. Its tools include a reduction onto the reaction support, a sign-count gate (m peaks need at least 2m − 1 sign changes among the residues), an exact response to redistributing a fixed reactivity budget, and a continuum bridge built from refined two-dimensional lattice ladders and off-lattice Brownian dynamics. The headline conclusion: folds seen on coarse grids escape to the boundary of the admissible region in the continuum. Related work in progress looks at encounters with several reactive zones.
- 4 Jul 2026 · **An interactive course for one’s own paper** (为自己的论文做一门交互课) — Completed. To understand the fold paper from the ground up, a single-file offline course was built around it: ten chapters that start from undergraduate analysis and linear algebra, build double-peak intuition from walker histograms, show how negative mode weights create peaks, and end with a slider for the sink’s strength that breaks the saddle-node fold live. Every chapter has self-tests. It is a study tool rather than course material — and the seed of the explainer in this chapter.
- 5 Jul 2026 · **46 theorems, checked by machine** (46 条定理，由机器核验) — Completed. The exact algebra of the fold paper — from Chebyshev product identities and the rank-one determinant to the closed-form splitting probability and the minimal three-mode theorem — was formalised in Lean 4, a proof assistant, with its mathlib library: 46 theorems across seven modules, with no ‘sorry’ (Lean’s placeholder for a missing proof) and only Lean’s three standard axioms. Numerical constants and analytic limits were left out of scope on purpose and checked numerically instead. Metrics: Theorems 46; Lean modules 7.
- 30 Jul 2026 · **Geometry-controlled folds: the double-peak paper** (几何控制的折叠：双峰论文) — Submitted to Physical Review E · Jul 2026. ‘Geometry-controlled folds of first-passage-time bimodality under localized absorption’ was submitted to Physical Review E as a single-author regular article on 30 July 2026. It is the first mathematics paper of the PhD and the capstone of the double-peak line: the geometry of a localized absorber decides whether a second arrival peak exists at all, and the peak is lost through a saddle-node fold whose location can be computed exactly. Every figure on this site that shows the effect comes from simulations written for this site, not from the manuscript. Links: [Research atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/)
- 13 Aug 2026 – 25 Aug 2026 · **Programming the number of peaks** (让峰的个数可以编程) — Completed. For a reacting Brownian pair swept past stripes of catalyst, a first theorem (August 2026) showed that a small enough budget split across m stripes yields exactly m reaction-time peaks. A campaign of about 325 million simulated walkers tested it: all 48 cells of the two-stripe phase diagram gave exactly two peaks, a five-peak demonstration put five peaks at their designed times, and a three-dimensional spot check passed unchanged. An explicit bound on the admissible budget was then sharpened by 692 orders of magnitude, and the finite-dimensional core was formalised in Lean 4 (138 audited declarations, no ‘sorry’). Metrics: Simulated walkers ≈ 325 million; Two-stripe cells exactly bimodal 48 / 48; Bound sharpened by 692 orders of magnitude. Links: [Reproduction archive](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes)
- 8 Sep 2026 – 26 Sep 2026 · **The public reproduction archive: code, proofs and records** (公开复现仓库：代码、证明与数据记录) — Live. Everything behind the fixed-budget paper is public and checkable: simulation, analysis and plotting code, machine-readable numerical records, interval-arithmetic certificates, the sources for Lean 4, the proof assistant, and the job records from Isambard 3 (a UK national supercomputer), each tied to SHA-256 manifests. Five releases went out between 8 and 26 September 2026 as the paper was rebuilt — about 1,466 files in the latest, including 100 Python scripts, 27 Lean files and 1,198 JSON records. Anyone can re-run the numbers without asking. Metrics: Releases 5 (v1.0.0 → v1.3.0); Files in v1.3.0 ≈ 1,466. Links: [Repository](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes) · [Release v1.3.0](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes/releases/tag/v1.3.0)
- 23 Sep 2026 · **Programmable multimodality: the fixed-budget paper** (可编程多峰：固定预算论文) — Manuscript in preparation. ‘Programmable multimodality and saddle-node loss of reaction-time peaks under a fixed catalyst budget’ is a single-author manuscript in preparation. A fixed amount of static catalyst, split into thin stripes along the path of a reacting Brownian pair, programs the reaction-time density: at weak noise each stripe removes a fixed fraction of the arriving pairs — a stick-breaking law — so there is exactly one peak per stripe, and designs with prescribed peak times and weights exist, are locally unique and can be found by Newton’s method. Fixed-width stripes can instead lose a late peak through a saddle-node bifurcation, certified by interval arithmetic in test cases. The finite-dimensional and calculus core is checked in Lean 4; the stochastic parts are proved by hand. Links: [Reproduction archive](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes)

## 02 · Skipping the IME? — First AI paper · UKAIRS 2026, the UK AI Research Symposium (跳过输入法？——第一篇 AI 论文 · 英国 AI 研究研讨会（UKAIRS 2026）)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/ai/skipping-the-ime/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/ai/skipping-the-ime/

Can AI agents read raw pinyin (romanised Chinese)? The Edinburgh poster says: for routine prompts, yes; homophones need the key word in characters.

Why it matters: Many languages are typed through an input method — software that turns typed letters into characters — or a romanisation: pinyin (romanised Chinese), Japanese romaji, Arabizi. Knowing where meaning survives the shortcut tells people when they can skip that step with an AI agent.

_Fig. 2 — Toneless pinyin as a walk that can end at the wrong word._

- 31 May 2026 · **The key finding: toneless pinyin erases homophones** (核心发现：无声调拼音抹掉同音字) — Completed. Three adversarial tasks hinge on words that collapse without tones: shu alone is 书 ‘book’, 树 ‘tree’, 输 ‘lose’ and 熟 ‘ripe’. Native characters scored 1.00, and so did the mixed workflow — instructions in pinyin, critical terms in characters. Clean pinyin, unspaced pinyin and pinyin with typos all averaged 0.333: the agent left the answer in pinyin or picked the wrong character. The one task that survived, 买 ‘buy’ against 卖 ‘sell’, was saved by 入 ‘in’ and 出 ‘out’. The mixed prompt still needs an estimated 0.815 of the native keystrokes; typing effort itself was not measured. Metrics: Native characters · mixed 1.00 · 1.00; Pinyin only (clean, no-space, typo) 0.333.
- 25 Feb 2026 · **An AI-native way of doing mathematics** (一种 AI 原生的做数学方式) — Ongoing. Across the first-passage line a repeatable loop took shape: AI models propose derivations and code, separate agents attack the claims, numerical computation acts as the arbiter, and exact algebra is machine-checked in Lean 4, a proof assistant. The documented cases include proposed formulas that failed numerical checks and were discarded, a repository-grounded audit that caught errors an outside model could not see, and multi-round reviews — up to about sixty agents in a single audit — before each submission. The principle in one line: AI can generate more scientific possibilities; the research skill is deciding which ones deserve belief. Metrics: Agents in one audit ≈ 60; Lean-checked theorems (fold paper) 46. Links: [Research atlas](https://zhouyi-xiaoxiao.github.io/valley-k-small/) · [Reproduction archive](https://github.com/zhouyi-xiaoxiao/prescribed-reaction-time-modes)
- May 2026 · **A research line that bends toward AI** (一条弯向 AI 的研究线) — Ongoing. Alongside first-passage research on random walks, the PhD work broadened during 2026 toward AI: evaluating AI agents built on large language models, human–AI interaction and multilingual input, and using multi-model AI workflows as research instruments — adversarial audits whose disagreements are settled by computation. The habit carries straight over: measure the hidden route, then refuse to believe the number until something independent confirms it. The UKAIRS 2026 acceptance is its first peer-reviewed AI output.
- 5 May 2026 – 6 May 2026 · **GOSIM Paris 2026** (GOSIM 巴黎 2026) — Attended. Attended GOSIM Paris 2026, ‘The Agentic AI Convergence’, at Station F, the Paris start-up campus, on 5–6 May. The takeaway, written up afterwards: open-source agent ecosystems are moving away from model showcases toward tool interoperability, model serving, edge deployment, production systems and trustworthy workflows — the same direction the evaluation work was heading. Links: [GOSIM Paris 2026](https://paris2026.gosim.org/)
- 28 May 2026 · **ime-eval: a harness for keyboard-friendly prompting** (ime-eval：键盘友好提示的评测框架) — Completed. ime-eval is the instrument behind the study. It drives real command-line coding agents rather than raw APIs, pairs every native-script prompt with keyboard-friendly variants — clean pinyin, no spaces, light typos, initials, and mixed prompts that keep key terms in native script — and defines profiles for eight input styles, from Japanese romaji and Vietnamese keyboard input to Hinglish, Arabizi, Russian transliteration, Greeklish and Korean. Hard rules from day one: configurations generated automatically, dry-run by default, results written once, and sandboxes that keep answers from leaking to the agent. Named here, not yet public. Metrics: Input styles configured 8; Pilot prompt variants 144.
- 28 May 2026 – 9 Jun 2026 · **A relay of three models, refereed by a human** (三个模型接力，一个人当裁判) — Completed. The study ran as a relay between AI systems. An orchestrating model wrote each phase brief; a coding agent implemented and ran it; a third, independent agent audited readiness before any real call was spent — for the homophone phase it returned ‘safe to run’. Every phase ended with a state-and-decision packet handed back to the orchestrator, and every step was committed to git. The human role was the architect’s: choose the phases, authorise the spend, carry the baton. Metrics: Independent readiness audits 4.
- 29 May 2026 – 30 May 2026 · **Four calls, four bugs, then a perfect score** (四次调用、四处程序错误，然后拿到满分) — Completed. Before any model call was spent, the harness was hardened: leakage-neutral work directories, an environment-gated switch for real runs with a hard cap on calls, preflight checks and deterministic scoring, each reviewed by an independent audit. The first real smoke test took four authorised calls and exposed four invocation bugs — relative schema paths, a blocked input stream and the strict rules of structured output. Once they were fixed, the pipeline answered correctly and scored 1.0. The test suite grew from 47 to 87 along the way. Metrics: Calls to first success 4; Bugs found 4.
- 30 May 2026 · **Catching a silent duplicate** (抓住一个隐形的重复) — Completed. A zero-cost audit of all 24 pilot tasks found that the ‘abbreviation’ condition produced prompts byte-for-byte identical to clean romanisation on three tasks — one Chinese, two Vietnamese — which would have silently wasted real calls. A deterministic, script-aware transform now renders syllable initials for Chinese, Japanese and Korean (so ‘shang dian li’ becomes ‘sdl’), and the variant lock records a digest of every rendered prompt, so that even a code-only change is caught by drift checks.
- 31 May 2026 · **A negative result: restoring the Chinese first made it worse** (反直觉：先还原成中文，反而更糟) — Completed. A small twelve-call repetition reproduced the lower score for abbreviations: direct answers to pinyin-initial prompts averaged 0.444 against 1.0 for native prompts. A ‘normalise, then answer’ wrapper did not rescue it. The mean fell to 0.333 because the model judged the initials too lossy and declined to answer in all three repetitions — turning confident wrong output into honest abstention. Native prompts were unaffected. It is a negative result, and it stayed in the paper. Metrics: Direct vs normalise-first 0.444 vs 0.333.
- 31 May 2026 · **Six input shapes: a ceiling, then a cliff** (六种写法：先撞天花板，再遇悬崖) — Completed. An arithmetic task came back correct under all six input shapes — good evidence that the plumbing worked, but a saturated test. A constraint-following task discriminated: clean pinyin, pinyin without spaces, pinyin with typos and a mixed prompt with English technical terms all returned the required three-item JSON array (a list format a program can read directly), while pinyin initials recovered the topic but lost the structure and scored 0.333. Under a placeholder keystroke model the initials needed an estimated 0.39 of the native keystrokes: a large estimated saving, and a measured loss in quality. Metrics: Initials on the formatting task 0.333 (native 1.00).
- 8 Jun 2026 · **A second agent, the same boundary** (换一个智能体，边界依旧) — Completed. Nine real calls to Claude Code on the same three homophone tasks reproduced the pattern exactly: native and mixed prompts scored 1.00, clean pinyin averaged 0.333. The pinyin ‘shi shi jian yan’, for example, came back as 实时检验 (‘real-time check’) for both items, instead of 事实检验 (‘fact check’) and 实施检验 (‘implementation check’). Two earlier batches were excluded as infrastructure failures rather than counted. The check made the finding cross-agent — reported in the paper as a small check, not a model comparison. Metrics: Valid calls 9.
- 8 Jun 2026 · **When the tool changes underneath: pin the model** (工具在脚下悄悄变了：钉死模型版本) — Completed. A prepared 48-call boundary study, with a new glossary condition, returned an error on every call. For reproducibility the harness ignored the command-line tool’s user configuration, so it fell back to a built-in default model that the signed-in account could not use. The batch was reported as a failure rather than scored as data; the model was then pinned explicitly and a one-call smoke confirmed the fix. The audit trail surfaced a second lesson: the exact model behind the earlier successful phases had not been recorded. Product tools change underneath you — pin exact model IDs.
- 8 Jun 2026 · **The UKAIRS paper: prompting AI agents in pinyin (romanised Chinese)** (UKAIRS 论文：用拼音向 AI 智能体下指令) — Submitted. ‘Skipping the IME? Keyboard-Friendly Multilingual Prompting for LLM Agents’ went to UKAIRS 2026, the UK AI Research Symposium, on 8 June: a two-page paper in the Emerging Research track, under the theme of synergistic human–AI collaboration, typeset so that the Chinese examples render inside an ACM template. It reports 48 valid text-only zh-CN calls — 39 to Codex and 9 to Claude Code, two AI coding agents — and proposes a design rule: skipping the IME (the input method) may be fine for routine scaffolding, but exact names, domain terms and homophones need native-script anchoring. Authors: Xiaoxiao Zhouyi and Yanzhen Li, University of Bristol. Metrics: Valid calls 48 (Codex 39 + Claude Code 9); Pages 2.
- 9 Jun 2026 · **Scaling to eight languages** (扩展到八种语言) — Planned. The next study was built before a single call was spent: 44 tasks across eight languages (264 prompt variants), split into high-risk exact-script tasks and controls; a fixed matrix of frontier models; a statistics engine with paired bootstrap confidence intervals; and generators for every table and figure. An adversarial audit from eight native-fluency perspectives replaced four homophone pairs that did not truly collapse. The main run is waiting on a go/no-go decision, so there are no multilingual results yet — and none are claimed. Metrics: Tasks · languages · variants 44 · 8 · 264.
- 30 Jun 2026 – 1 Jul 2026 · **Triangulated audit: three minds and a calculator** (三角审计：三个大脑加一台计算器) — Shipped. A reusable audit skill that attacks a research package from three angles over several rounds — a multi-agent workflow with access to the repository and tools, a strong external model, and a numerical and empirical arbiter — and settles every disagreement between models by computation rather than authority. The audit that motivated it showed why: a strong external model got a formula and a threshold wrong that the other participants got right; only the union plus the arbiter was complete; and a mistaken refutation forced a certification that made the result stronger.
- 11 Aug 2026 · **What the next version will measure** (下一版要测什么) — Planned. The next study will measure typing effort and answer quality together, with a small typing experiment instead of a keystroke model; add about thirty homophone tasks with graded ambiguity; record the exact version of every model; and test why normalising the input first can lower quality. Claims will stay within the languages and tasks actually tested — the eight-language harness is built for the broader test.
- 11 Aug 2026 · **Accepted at UKAIRS 2026: the first AI paper** (UKAIRS 2026 录用：第一篇 AI 论文) — Accepted. On 11 August 2026 UKAIRS accepted the paper for a poster session in the Emerging Research track. The reviews found the question genuinely interesting, the artefact useful-looking and the inclusivity angle worth pursuing, and recommended leading with the ‘shi shi’ example and the three-layer analysis — encoding change, compression, tone loss. It is the first peer-reviewed AI paper, first-authored. Links: [Poster list](https://ukairs2026.eventsadmin.com/i/PosterSessions)
- 28 Aug 2026 · **Poster #181, Wednesday 25 November** (181 号海报，11 月 25 日周三) — Scheduled. The organisers assigned the poster to Wednesday 25 November 2026, 13:15–14:15, in Lunch & Poster Session 3, and sent the presentation guidance. The public poster list shows it as #181 under ‘F. Synergistic Human–AI Collaboration’, Emerging Research, Xiaoxiao Zhouyi, University of Bristol. Links: [Poster list](https://ukairs2026.eventsadmin.com/i/PosterSessions)
- 24 Nov 2026 – 25 Nov 2026 · **UK AI Research Symposium (UKAIRS 2026), Edinburgh** (英国 AI 研究研讨会（UKAIRS 2026），爱丁堡) — Scheduled · poster on 25 Nov. UKAIRS 2026, the UK AI Research Symposium, runs on 24–25 November 2026 at the John McIntyre Conference Centre in Edinburgh; poster #181 is up on Wednesday 25 November, 13:15–14:15. The plan, written into the paper, is a side-by-side demo — the native prompt, its keyboard-friendly variant, the agent’s response, the grade and the effort estimate — so that visitors can toggle from routine prompts to homophone traps and watch where meaning collapses. Chapter 02 of this site is an early version of that demo. Links: [Poster list](https://ukairs2026.eventsadmin.com/i/PosterSessions)

## 03 · The Engine Room — R&D Scientist (AI) at Yuexin International, a cloud-communications company (引擎室——阅信国际 · AI 研发)

https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/work/engine-room/ · https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/zh/work/engine-room/

Since June 2026 at Yuexin International: five AI systems built and live in four months — a gateway, a governed platform, a staff assistant.

Why it matters: The aim: move the company from trying AI to using it every day — safely, with governance built in, and with a person confirming before anything is sent, shared or approved.

_Fig. 3 — Requests as walkers; governance rules decide where each one stops._

- Jun 2026 · **R&D Scientist (AI), Yuexin International** (阅信国际 · AI 研发) — Ongoing. Role: R&D Scientist (AI), Yuexin International. Joined in June 2026, alongside the PhD, at a company whose business spans messaging, voice and AI. Of the three strands, the widest is habit rather than software: AI training for every department, and the scattered pilots gathered into one programme in July. The entries below are what got built. Links: [Yuexin International on LinkedIn](https://www.linkedin.com/company/yuexin-international)
- 11 Mar 2026 – 21 Mar 2026 · **A Chinese SMS classifier that runs on the device** (在设备上运行的中文短信分类模型) — Completed. An on-device classifier for Chinese SMS, built for a cloud-communications company: a large language model acted as the teacher, labelling examples, and its judgement was distilled into a lightweight student that sorts each message into verification codes, notifications or marketing in well under a millisecond. Three student models were compared on a labelled test set; a support-vector machine (a classic, lightweight classifier) won, with a macro-F1 of 0.91 (an average score that weights every category equally). Fraud detection was deliberately left out of scope. Metrics: Macro-F1 (class-averaged score) 0.91.
- 25 May 2026 – 29 May 2026 · **A thesis: communication is the execution layer for AI agents** (一个论断：通信是 AI 智能体的执行层) — Completed. In May 2026, in a series of memos and one-pagers, an argument took shape: communication becomes the execution layer for AI agents. An agent that can reach people through the channels they already use — messages, notifications — is an agent that can finish a job. It is a personal thesis rather than company strategy, and it explains why a first-passage mathematician ended up building AI systems inside a cloud-communications company whose core business is SMS.
- 1 Jun 2026 · **Feishu connectors that let AI agents work inside the workspace** (飞书连接器：让智能体进入工作台) — Live. A suite of MCP connectors (MCP is an open protocol that lets AI call outside tools) that lets coding agents work inside the company’s workspace in Feishu (also known as Lark, a workplace chat-and-docs suite) — documents, sheets, chats, meeting minutes and approvals — with scoped permissions, acting as the signed-in person rather than as an all-powerful bot. Written documentation made it something colleagues could install, not just a demo.
- 10 Jun 2026 – 13 Jun 2026 · **An internal AI gateway with single sign-on** (带飞书单点登录的内部 AI 网关) — Live. Within four days an open-source gateway for large language models (LLMs) became the company’s internal AI platform, the Yuexin Intelligent Open Platform. The gateway was chosen by reading the source code of two candidates rather than their brochures. The work covered a deployment runbook, white-labelling and full Chinese localisation of the admin interface, a mobile layout, and a self-service portal where colleagues sign in with Feishu (also known as Lark, a workplace chat-and-docs suite), get a key and see their own usage. Router retries, fallbacks and per-member budgets followed, and a pre-launch audit of model and permission boundaries closed the week.
- 14 Jul 2026 – 22 Jul 2026 · **Pulling the AI pilots into one programme** (把零散的 AI 试点收拢成一个项目) — Plan drafted. In July 2026 the company’s scattered AI pilots were pulled into one programme: a drafted plan, pilots and department-level AI training. The training itself is described in Chapter 04.
- 22 Jul 2026 · **A morning briefing written by an agent** (由智能体撰写的晨报) — Live. A daily agent that turns official public procurement notices into leads: it reads each notice, pulls out what is being bought and what is required, and writes a brief that a person can follow up. Everything with consequences — registering, buying documents, pricing, submitting — stays with people.
- 25 Jul 2026 – 31 Jul 2026 · **An enterprise platform for governed AI access** (企业 AI 统一接入与治理平台) — Live. The company’s enterprise AI unified-access and governance platform went from local build to live in a week, launching on 31 July 2026. It is a self-built portal over an open-source gateway: organisations, teams and virtual keys, model allow-lists, budgets and usage, a data-loss-prevention hook and an audit hash-chain, with the gateway’s own admin interface closed to the internet. Around launch it went through several rounds of adversarial review by parallel AI agents; privacy-canary checks that planted synthetic identifiers and confirmed none survived in storage or logs; and formal production acceptance, with a receipt for every model.
- 21 Sep 2026 · **Yuexin AI Assistant — web and Windows** (阅信 AI 助手——网页版与 Windows 版) — Live. In one day, an assistant for company staff was built and launched on the company’s model gateway. Colleagues sign in with Feishu and are provisioned automatically, with a personal monthly quota and self-serve API keys. The web app streams its answers, folds away the model’s reasoning, renders Markdown and maths, accepts images and has light and dark themes; a Windows desktop client shipped alongside it, with a download page. Before release it went through three parallel security reviews and an independent review by a second model.
- 23 Sep 2026 · **From chat window to desktop agent** (从聊天窗口到桌面智能体) — In development. The desktop assistant is being rebuilt as a coding and office agent: an open-source agent engine underneath, a Yuexin interface on top. Planned for the next rounds: a built-in browser and terminal, scheduled tasks, skills, and acting in Feishu, the company’s workplace suite, on the person’s behalf — with a confirmation before every send, share or approval. It is still in development; these are plans, not shipped features.

Giving a cloud-communications company an AI-era face: a logo system, materials for two trade shows (MWC Shanghai, WWC Madrid), a 93-minute AI primer.

_Fig. 4 — A trade floor as a field of targets, reached one conversation at a time._

Its argument in one line: a skill is not a longer prompt — it is a reusable instruction manual for the AI.

- 13 Jul 2026 – 31 Jul 2026 · **Hands-on AI agent training for operations teams** (面向运营团队的 AI 智能体实战培训) — Completed. Ran the operations team’s second round of hands-on agent training as lead trainer and technical judge. Each colleague demonstrated a real task running through an AI agent and was scored on time saved, quality, human review and reusability; the sessions covered browser and computer use, cross-app automation, memory and skills, scheduling and alerts. The cases were written up for reuse, and a case-based ‘AI work assistant’ boot camp was designed for the sales department.
- 5 Aug 2026 · **‘From SMS to Intelligent Channels’: a 93-minute primer on AI models** (《从短信到智能通道》：93 分钟大模型入门课) — Delivered. An in-person AI fundamentals session for technical and business staff on 5 August 2026, recorded at 1 hour 33 minutes, that explained how the large-language-model industry works through the SMS business: a Chinese SMS is billed per 70 characters, a model per token (the unit of text a model reads and writes), so the team’s instinct for counting characters transfers directly. It ran from the value chain and the cost of tokens to retrieval, agents, hallucination and private deployment — and the six questions customers always ask. The materials — a 24-slide deck, a 60-minute script and a handbook with an 81-term glossary, self-tests and customer-dialogue drills — were finalised the next day. Metrics: Length 93 min.
- 5 Sep 2026 – 8 Sep 2026 · **‘Intelligence. Delivered.’ — print and digital kit for a Madrid trade show** (「智能，送达」——马德里展会的印刷与数字物料) — Shipped. In three design rounds over four days (5–8 September), the trade-show kit for the Wholesale World Congress (WWC, a telecoms trade show in Madrid): a series of five one-pager types, opened by an English sheet headlined ‘Intelligence. Delivered.’; then — after the team’s prep meeting — three double-sided A4 leaflets in English and Chinese with one QR code per sheet, an English company introduction, a supplier questionnaire and four business cards for the delegation. Everything was built through an HTML-to-PDF pipeline, and every QR code was decode-tested before the print files went out on 8 September. Metrics: Design rounds 3; One-pager types 5; Double-sided leaflets 3 × 2 languages; Business cards 4.
- 7 Sep 2026 – 8 Sep 2026 · **‘People. Connected.’ — a contact site for the delegation** (「人，相连」——代表团的联系网站) — Live. A contact microsite for the Wholesale World Congress delegation, reached from a 19 mm QR code on each business card: a page per person with messaging, LinkedIn, email, website and save-contact links, plus a browser-based card editor so that each person can maintain their own. It went live on the company’s connect subdomain and was decode-tested card by card.
- 11 Sep 2026 · **An interactive SMS market map** (交互式短信市场地图) — Live. An interactive, bilingual map of how enterprises buy SMS and where delivery really succeeds. It follows one text message from a business to a phone — who carries it, which way the money and the delivery receipts travel, and what ‘delivered’ can mean — then maps who buys, what they need and how they choose. It began as a whiteboard sketch and became a dependency-free web page the same day, revised after three AI review passes on content, usability and release safety. The version on this site was rebuilt for a general reader. Links: [Open the SMS market map →](https://zhouyixiaoxiao.com/lab/sms-market-map/)

A concept for an AI and programming literacy escape room: an overconfident assistant hands the players code that looks right, and the only way out is to verify it — write the failing test, find the evidence — instead of trusting a confident answer. It is the verify-everything habit of the research, turned into a game for students.
